thread.title: Harvard Sold Apple Stock and Dodged a Bullet - Barron's

title: Harvard Sold Apple Stock and Dodged a Bullet - Barron's
text:
Harvard Sold Apple Stock and Dodged a Bullet By Nov. 16, 2018 7:00 a.m. ET Order Reprints Harvard University. Photograph by Scott Eisen/Getty Images Text size
Harvard University’s endowment has a history of underperforming . Its return of 8.1% for fiscal 2017 was bested by every other Ivy League school and trounced by the 12.7% average posted by college and university endowments.
Fiscal 2018, ended on June 30, was slightly better, as the world’s biggest university endowment posted a 10% return . Still, it lagged behind peers in the first full year that N.P. “Narv” Narvekar has helmed Harvard Management Co., or HMC, the entity that manages the endowment.
Narvekar pulled off at least one savvy investing move in the first fiscal quarter ended on Sept. 30. He slashed the stake in Apple (ticker: AAPL) by 411,039 shares, to 107,907 shares, according to HMC’s latest filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission. The 79% reduction meant that Harvard was less exposed to the stock’s recent dive on worries that demand is flagging for the latest iPhone models.
Apple shares have slid 15.2% since the end of the third quarter. HMC saved $14.1 million by selling those Apple shares ahead of the slump, Barron’s calculates. That’s the same as the estimated 2018-19 tuition of $46,340 for 304 undergraduate students.
Read More: Apple’s iPhone Revenue Is Poised to Fall Next Year
“HMC does not comment on specific investments,” the entity said, declining to make Narvekar available for this article.
HMC had a minor windfall by cutting back on Microsoft (MSFT), which was co-founded by Harvard dropout Bill Gates. The endowment sliced off 37% of its holdings in the software giant to end the third quarter with 881,533 shares. Microsoft has slipped 6.2% since the end of the third quarter, so HMC sold those shares before they could drop $3.5 million in value.
Not all of HMC’s moves were good, though. It drastically increased its holdings in Facebook (FB), which was founded by another Harvard dropout, Mark Zuckerberg. HMC increased its investment in the social network more than 22 times, to 328,681 shares, in the third quarter. The additional 314,821 shares, if HMC still owns them, have dropped 12.5% in value since the end of the third quarter; that represents a drop of $6.5 million in value in the added shares alone. Morale among Facebook employees has been falling as well, and founders of acquired companies have been leaving .
One new investment hasn’t been panning out this quarter. HMC initiated a position in genetic-testing firm Natera (NTRA) after buying 638,979 shares in the third quarter. The stock has slumped, however. HMC’s Natera stake was valued at $15.3 million at the end of September, but after a 33% slide so far in the fourth quarter, those shares are valued at $10.3 million, down $5.0 million.
